Risk 1

The model confidently makes things up — a human must check the answer

45%
of AI assistant answers about news had a significant issue (EBU/BBC, 22 broadcasters, October 2025)
2 190
court decisions worldwide where AI-invented citations were found (D. Charlotin’s database, October 2026)
$5 000
fine for lawyers in Mata v. Avianca (US, 2023): they cited cases ChatGPT made up
1
AI answered
confident and fluent — not a sign of truth
→
2
Find the source
the law, report, company site, document
→
3

numbers, names, dates, links, quotes

You send it
and you are responsible for it
Rule: check numbers, names, links, laws and quotes from an AI answer against the original source. The sender is responsible, not the AI.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 15 • Responsible AI03 / 17
Risk 2

A leak starts with one pasted file: decide in advance which data may go where

Public
website texts, published documents
→
any AI tool
Internal
plans, internal emails
→
company-approved AI only
Confidential
customer personal data, contracts
→
only approved work AI, with permission; never a personal one
Passwords, keys, tokens — never, into any AI
Samsung, 2023: engineers pasted company source code into ChatGPT; the company then temporarily banned generative AI tools on work devices.
Grok, 2025: the share button made chats public — Forbes found over 370,000 conversations in Google.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 15 • Responsible AI04 / 17
Plans

Same model, different rules: personal and business plans treat data differently

ChatGPT Free / Plus / Pro
your chats may be used for training unless you switch it off: Settings → Data controls
Claude Free / Pro / Max
since August 2025 you choose; if allowed, kept for up to 5 years
ChatGPT Business/Enterprise · Claude for Work · Gemini in Workspace
do not train on company data by default
Work data goes only into the company’s business account. A personal ChatGPT or Claude is not for customer documents, even a paid one.

Risk 3

A video call with “the CFO” can be fake: verify money requests through another channel

$25 M
Arup, Hong Kong, 2024: an employee transferred money after a video call where the “CFO” and colleagues were deepfakes — fake videos and voices
1
A call from “the CFO”
face and voice are familiar — it may be a deepfake
2
Urgent and secret
“transfer today, tell no one” — the main sign of fraud
3
Stop
end the call, pay nothing
4
Call back yourself
on a known number, not the one in the message; or ask for the code word

Risk 4

Excessive agency: an agent does whatever it has rights to — even if you did not want it to

9 seconds
PocketOS, April 2026: an AI agent in the Cursor code editor found a stray access key in a file and deleted the production database and its backups; about 30 hours of downtime
Replit
July 2025: an agent deleted a production database during a declared code freeze
1
A task for the agent
an ordinary request in Cursor
→
2
A key in a file
the agent found access nobody meant to give
→
3
Database and backups deleted
in 9 seconds, without asking a human
→
4
~30 hours of downtime
customers without the service
Rules from L11–L12: least privilege · no production passwords or keys near the agent · human confirmation for deletion and money · backups kept separately.

Bias

AI repeats the biases in its data: CVs that differed only in the name were ranked differently

University of Washington study (2024): AI ranked CVs that differed only in the name.
How often the model preferred the CV with such a name
White-associated names
85%
Black-associated names
9%
Male-associated names
52%
Female-associated names
11%
050100%
In the remaining comparisons neither group was preferred.
Rule: decisions about people — hiring, credit, dismissal — AI may prepare, but a human decides. Laws are moving the same way (slides 11–12).
GenAI Basics • Lesson 15 • Responsible AI09 / 17
Labelling

Laws already require labelling AI content — deepfakes first; technology helps: invisible marks and signatures

SynthID (Google)
an invisible mark in pixels, sound and text; you can check an image in the Gemini app
C2PA Content Credentials
signed “who made it, with what” metadata; lost on a screenshot
No mark ≠ made by a human
and a mark does not prove the content is true
Labelling is already required: China (from 1.09.2025), Kazakhstan (from 18.01.2026), EU — Art. 50 (from 2.08.2026). Russia: law 243-FZ, labelling provisions from 1.03.2027 — whether mandatory is still disputed.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 15 • Responsible AI10 / 17
EU AI Act

The EU AI Act applies in stages — most of it is in force, high-risk rules from 2027

2.02.2025
prohibited practices
2.08.2025
general-purpose models (like ChatGPT)
2.08.2026
most rules + labelling (Art. 50)
2.12.2026
ban on “nudification” generators
2.12.2027
“high-risk” — systems deciding about people: hiring, credit, education
Fines: up to €35M or 7% of turnover for prohibited practices; up to €15M or 3% for the rest, including labelling.
It also applies to companies outside the EU if their AI is used in the EU.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 15 • Responsible AI11 / 17
Our region

Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Russia have already passed AI laws or amendments — with a lot in common

Uzbekistan
law ZRU-1115 (January 2026): decisions on people’s rights not on AI alone; AI ethics rules (from 17.06.2026)
Kazakhstan
Law “On Artificial Intelligence” (from 18.01.2026): manipulation ban, labelling
Russia
AI law 243-FZ (from 1.09.2026); labelling provisions from 1.03.2027, mandatory status disputed
US · UK
no single law; separate state and sector rules
In common: a human is accountable for decisions and personal data is protected; Kazakhstan already requires labelling AI content.
This is an overview, not legal advice: check details with your company’s lawyers.

Team rules

AI rules for a team fit on one page: four points

Approved tools
a list of AI allowed for work, and business accounts
Data traffic light
what goes anywhere, what only into work AI, what only with permission
A human checks
numbers, links, decisions about people — before sending
Labels and incidents
label AI content; where to report a leak
